html:
The 1970 Pakistani general election, held on 7 December 1970, was the first nationwide vote in Pakistan's history. It gave the Awami League of East Pakistan an outright majority and set off the crisis that split the country.

The military ruler, General Yahya Khan, had promised a vote to hand power back to civilians. The seats were divided by population, so East Pakistan, the larger wing, got a majority of the National Assembly. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman ran on his Six Points, a plan for wide autonomy for the East. A great cyclone in November had delayed some polling there.

The Awami League won almost every seat in the East, 160 out of 162, and so had a majority in the whole assembly. In the West the Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's Pakistan Peoples Party won the most seats, but not enough to rule.

The army and the western leaders were not ready to see Mujib as prime minister. Talks failed, the assembly was put off in March 1971, and the result of the election led to Operation Searchlight and the Bangladesh Liberation War.
sum: The 1970 Pakistani general election, held on 7 December 1970, was the first nationwide vote in Pakistan's history. It gave the Awami League of East Pakistan an outright majority and set off the crisis that split the country.
